title: Linkability of sensor telemetry data
description: Continuous collection of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps enables linking of data points to reconstruct user movement patterns, daily routines, and health behaviors over time.
assumptions: Data is stored and processed in a way that maintains temporal and spatial correlations

title: Identifiability through biometric and location data
description: The combination of GPS position, timestamps, and biometric data (heart rate) can be used to uniquely identify the user, especially when cross-referenced with other data sources.
assumptions: Data is accessible to parties who could perform identification analysis

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensor data
description: Sensor telemetry data transmitted from user to wearable device could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Data transmission and storage mechanisms may have security vulnerabilities

title: Data aggregation revealing sensitive patterns
description: Aggregation of multiple data types (heart rate, steps, GPS, timestamps) enables inference of sensitive information beyond individual data points, such as health conditions, lifestyle habits, and location preferences.
assumptions: Multiple data streams are combined and analyzed together

title: User unawareness of data collection scope
description: Users may not be fully aware of the extent of data being collected, how long it is retained, who has access to it, or how it may be used for secondary purposes.
assumptions: Privacy notices may be unclear or users may not read them thoroughly

title: Device ID and GPS traces enable user identification
description: The wearable device transmits device ID and GPS traces to the companion app. These data elements can be used to uniquely identify the user and track their movements, creating identifiability risks.
assumptions: Device ID is unique per device/user; GPS traces contain precise location data

title: Sensitive personal data disclosed in transmission
description: Exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps reveal sensitive personal information including location patterns, physical activity levels, and daily routines. This data disclosure occurs during the sync process.
assumptions: GPS and exercise data are considered sensitive personal information

title: Potential data minimality violation in sensor batch sync
description: The wearable device transfers complete sensor batches including GPS traces and exercise data. This may violate the minimality principle if all transmitted data is not strictly required for the companion app's functionality.
assumptions: Not all sensor data may be necessary for app operation; data minimality principle applies
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether all transmitted data is strictly necessary without knowing app requirements

title: User unawareness of data transmission scope
description: Users may not be fully aware of what sensor data (GPS traces, exercise sessions, device ID, timestamps) is being transmitted from the wearable to the companion app during sync operations.
assumptions: Users may not read detailed privacy policies or understand technical data flows

title: Linkability of health data to user identity
description: Calorie intake, meal, and weight data entered by the user can be linked to their personal identity through the companion app account, creating a linkable health profile.
assumptions: User account is tied to identifiable information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health information
description: Sensitive health data (calorie intake, meals, weight) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage in the companion app.
assumptions: Data transmission and storage may have security vulnerabilities

title: Aggregation of health data points
description: Multiple data entries (calories, meals, weight over time) can be aggregated to create a detailed health and lifestyle profile of the user beyond individual data points.
assumptions: App stores historical data entries

title: User unawareness of data sharing implications
description: The user may not be fully aware of how their health data is being collected, processed, shared with third parties, or used for purposes beyond their understanding.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not be fully understood by users

title: Limited user control over data processing
description: Once health data is entered into the app, the user may have limited ability to control how it is processed, shared, or retained by the system.
assumptions: App may have limited data control options for users

title: Excessive Health Data Collection
description: The companion app may collect and store more health data than necessary (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) violating the data minimality principle. This could include granular details that exceed what's needed for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: App collects detailed health metrics without clear justification for each data point

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Log Store
description: The health log store containing sensitive personal health data (weight, exercise, calorie intake) could be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, database vulnerabilities, or compromised credentials.
assumptions: Health log store has standard security controls that may be insufficient for sensitive health data

title: User Unawareness of Data Storage
description: Users may not be fully aware that their detailed health logs are being stored persistently in the health log store, including what specific data points are collected and how long they are retained.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain data storage practices for health information

title: Health Data Storage Compliance Risk
description: Storage of health-related personal data may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) regarding data protection, retention periods, and security requirements for sensitive health information.
assumptions: Health log store may not implement all required compliance measures for health data
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and specific health data classification

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The app writes GPS location traces with timestamps to the location history store. This may collect more location data than strictly necessary for the app's functionality, violating the minimality principle. Continuous location tracking could be considered avoidable data disclosure.
assumptions: Location tracking is continuous or more frequent than required for app functionality

title: Location Data Enables User Identification
description: GPS location traces with timestamps can be used to identify individuals, especially when combined with other data sources. Location history is highly identifying personal data.
assumptions: Location data is stored with sufficient granularity to identify individuals

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History Store
description: The location history store containing GPS traces and timestamps could be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or insider threats.
assumptions: Data store has access control mechanisms that could be bypassed or compromised

title: Users Unaware of Location Tracking Scope
description: Users may not be fully aware that their GPS location is being continuously tracked and stored with timestamps, or the extent of this data collection.
assumptions: Privacy notices do not clearly communicate the scope and frequency of location tracking

title: Location Data Enables Cross-Context Linking
description: Location history with timestamps can be linked to other data about the user across different contexts, enabling comprehensive profiling of user behavior and movements.
assumptions: Location data can be correlated with other user data in the system

title: Cross-session health data linkability
description: The Health Analytics Service reads calorie, weight, and exercise logs across multiple sessions, enabling the creation of comprehensive health profiles by linking data points over time. This aggregation allows correlation of health behaviors and conditions that could reveal sensitive patterns about individuals.
assumptions: The analytics service has access to session identifiers or timestamps that enable temporal correlation of health data

title: Excessive health data collection for analytics
description: The analytics service reads all calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions for health-condition analysis. This may violate the minimality principle if not all collected data is strictly necessary for the stated purpose, constituting implicit data disclosure beyond what users reasonably expect.
assumptions: The health-condition analysis may not require all historical health log data across all sessions
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether the analytics purpose genuinely requires all historical data or if data minimization could be applied

title: User unawareness of cross-session health analysis
description: Users may not be aware that their health logs (calorie, weight, exercise) are being read and analyzed across multiple sessions for health-condition analysis. This lack of transparency prevents informed consent about the scope of data processing.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate cross-session analytics capabilities

title: Cross-session location data linking
description: The Health Analytics Service queries location history across multiple sessions to derive daily routines and movement patterns, enabling linkage of disparate location data points into a comprehensive behavioral profile.
assumptions: Location history data contains sufficient granularity to enable meaningful pattern analysis across time periods.

title: Movement pattern identifiability
description: Derived daily routine and movement patterns from location history can serve as unique behavioral identifiers, potentially enabling re-identification of individuals even if direct identifiers are removed.
assumptions: Movement patterns are sufficiently unique to individuals to enable identification or re-identification.

title: Implicit disclosure through derived patterns
description: The analytics service derives sensitive information (daily routines, movement patterns) from location history that may reveal implicit personal data beyond what was explicitly collected, potentially violating data minimality principles.
assumptions: Derived patterns reveal information about users that they did not explicitly consent to share.

title: User unawareness of cross-session analysis
description: Users may not be aware that their location history is being analyzed across multiple sessions to derive behavioral patterns, limiting their ability to make informed consent decisions.
assumptions: Privacy notices do not clearly communicate cross-session pattern analysis capabilities.

title: Health analytics data disclosure during transmission
description: Inferred health insights (risk indicators, routine summaries, trend flags) transmitted from Health Analytics Service to Companion App could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties if transmission lacks proper encryption or security controls.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network between processes; assumes standard network security may not be sufficient for sensitive health data

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management for health data transmission
description: Transmission of sensitive health analytics data may not have adequate cybersecurity risk management controls that properly address privacy risks, potentially violating health data protection regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR).
assumptions: Health data is subject to regulatory requirements; assumes cybersecurity controls may not fully address privacy-specific risks

title: Identity disclosure through health inference data
description: Inferred health-condition risk indicators and trend flags could reveal or confirm the identity of the data subject when combined with other available information, especially if the app or analytics service is compromised.
assumptions: Health inference data is personally identifiable or can be linked to specific individuals

title: Unauthorized access to sensitive health risk indicators
description: The app dashboard displays inferred health condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) to the user. If the user's device is compromised, shared, or accessed by unauthorized parties, these sensitive health inferences could be disclosed to individuals who should not have access to this information.
assumptions: User device may be shared or compromised; no additional access controls beyond app login

title: User unawareness of inference methodology and accuracy
description: Users may not be aware of how the eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals were inferred, what data sources were used, the accuracy of these inferences, or the potential for false positives/negatives. This lack of transparency could lead to inappropriate health decisions based on misunderstood risk indicators.
assumptions: App may not provide clear explanations of inference algorithms or confidence levels

title: Non-compliance with health data regulations
description: Displaying inferred health condition indicators may violate health data protection regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) if proper consent, accuracy guarantees, or medical disclaimers are not in place. Inferred health risks may be considered medical data requiring specific compliance measures.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for displaying health inferences may not be fully addressed
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and specific implementation details

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: The full health and location dataset is explicitly transferred to an external cloud hosting provider (EE2). This represents a data disclosure across a system boundary to a third party. The minimality principle may be violated if all data in the 'full dataset' is not strictly required for the analytics service.
assumptions: The cloud provider is a legitimate third-party service; data transfer is intentional and by design.

title: Linkability of Health and Location Data at Cloud Provider
description: Health and location data sent to the cloud provider could be linked with other datasets the provider maintains or obtains, potentially creating comprehensive profiles of individuals that exceed the original purpose of the analytics service.
assumptions: The cloud provider may have access to or could obtain additional data about the same individuals.

title: Inference of Sensitive Information from Analytics Models
description: The cloud provider could potentially infer sensitive information about individuals from the analytics models and datasets transferred, including patterns in health conditions or location behaviors that were not explicitly disclosed.
assumptions: Analytics models contain sufficient information to enable inference attacks.

title: User Unawareness of Third-Party Data Transfer
description: Individuals whose health and location data is being processed may not be aware that their data is being transferred to and stored at a third-party cloud hosting provider, limiting their ability to make informed consent decisions.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate third-party data transfers or users may not read them.

title: Regulatory Compliance Risks for Health Data Transfer
description: Transferring health data to a third-party cloud provider may create compliance challenges with regulations such as HIPAA, GDPR, or other health data protection laws, particularly if the provider is in a different jurisdiction.
assumptions: The cloud provider's location and data handling practices may not fully align with applicable health data regulations.
uncertainty_note: Specific compliance requirements depend on jurisdiction and provider location, which are not specified in the flow description.
